 Judgment
The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 14.01.2022 at about 09.30 p.m, when the petitioner was riding a TVS Jupiter bearing No. (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 KA-04-HX-5277 on the extreme left side of the road, in front of Anupama School, Andrahalli Main Road, Bengaluru, at that time, a Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-13-EV-0241 driven by its rider at high speed,
in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle.
Due to this petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and scooter was damaged.

Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Suresh hospital, Bengaluru and Suguna hospital and after necessary treatment discharged with an advise for follow-up treatment and for complete bed rest and still he is continuing the follow-up treatment as per the advise of the doctor and so far he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.

Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 53 years and was doing Bonda Bajji Mixture business at Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/-
p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the aforesaid offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Byadarahalli Police (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 have registered a case against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared before this tribunal and filed objections.

04. Respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-13-EV-0241 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the offending Motor Cycle is not involved in the accident and said Motor Cycle was not at all involved in the alleged accident and there is a delay Suresh B.L vs Ravi M.J on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83288824/
2 of 08 days in lodging the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 complaint and no valid reasons assigned for the delay and the offending Motor Cycle was falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle, hospital authorities and the Police, to get compensation by this respondent and the claim petition was filed after lapse of 1 years 6 months from the date of accident and the rider of the Motor Cycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence, thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

sentences.text: The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.

05. Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -
ISSUES

01. Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 14.01.2022 at about 9.30 p.m, infront of Anupama School,
Andrahalli Main Road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EV-0241 by its rider as alleged in the petition ?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed his side evidence.
Ex . P.18
is marked by consent.

07. By way of rebuttal, despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.2 did nto lead evidence,
hence respondent No.2 side evidence is taken as nil.
08. Heard both sides.

The councel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the following citations:-
01. Civil Appeal No.1337-1338/2019 in a case of Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation V/s Vibhor Fialok and another,
02. MFA No.3153/2017 (MV-I) in a case of Krishna Murthy V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., and another,
03. MFA No.5553/2024 (MV-I) in a case of Anthoniswamy V/s Shanthi.C and another.

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In affirmative  Issue No.2
In partly affirmative
Issue No.3
As per final order  for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle by its rider, the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered at Byadarahalli Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/Sec 279, 337 of IPC and U/Sec 187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.2 shows that the petitioner himself lodged the complaint after 8 days of accident stating that due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle the accident was occurred and due to which he petitioner fell down and (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 sustained injuries and he explained reasons for delay stating that he took treatment in Suresh hospital and his right leg was bandaged, due to which he could not walk properly, hence he lodged belated complaint.
Ex.P.3 is Spot Mahazar showing the place of accident opposite to Anupama School, Andrahalli Main Road, Byadarahalli, Yeshwanthpur Hobli, Bengaluru, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.4 and 5 are IMV reports which discloses that involvement of both vehicles in the accident and petitioner's vehicle got damages on its right and left side.

Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which shows that the petitioner sustained abrasion over right knee and ligamental tear of right knee, out of which injury No.2 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Ex.P.7 is the important document of Investigation Officer.

After completion of the investigation filed Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle for the offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC and U/Sec 187 of IMV Act for the reasons after causing accident the rider without stopping his Motor Cycle fled away from the accident spot.
Ex.P.8 is Discharge summary shows that the petitioner sustained injury to right knee.
Ex.P.11 and 12 are the Driving licence and Aadhaar card of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 petitioner.
To disprove the petitioner case, the respondent No.2 did not lead any evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:-
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

sentences.text: Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 53 years and was doing Bonda Bajji Mixture business at Bengaluru and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m and has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not attend to his work, resulted in loss of earning, earning capacity and put to great financial hardship.
12. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not produced any other documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/-
(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.15,500/-.

13. According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief-examination that the petitioner has sustained right knee full thickness tear of anterior crucial ligament partial tear of posterior cruciate ligament with medial meniscal injury and he assessed permanent physical disability of 20% of right lower limb, which is 10% of whole body.
14.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-
The petitioner has produced Discharge summary at Ex.P.8 of Suresh hospital, Bengaluru, which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital only for one day.

During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.20,000/- under this head.
15. Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 per X-rays, MRI reports, MRI films and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.20,000/- under this head.
16. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.15,500/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for one day as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast one month.

Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.15,500/- (Rs.15,500/- x 1)
under this head.
17. Medical Expenses:-
The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.10 for Rs.53,109/- and Prescriptions as per Ex.P.9.
To disprove the medical bills, the respondent No.2 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.53,109/-
under this head.

5
18. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

19. Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is duty of petitioner to prove his age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Driving licence and Aadhaar card at Ex.P.11 and 12.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age for any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 05.06.1968 and the alleged accident was occurred on 14.01.2022.
Therefore, considering the said documents and police records and medical records, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 54 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is '11'.
20.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The doctor PW.2 has given disability of 20% and 10% pertaining to whole body.

In his cross-examination he admits that he has not treated the petitioner personally and he examined the petitioner for assessing the disability and the wounds are healed and petitioner not sustain any fracture and has not undergone any operation and he has not taken the opinion of the treated doctor and further admits that petitioner can do his work by sitting and it is little difficult to do work by standing and he can do his day to day routine activities with some difficulty.

However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, medical records and ratio laid down in the above said citations relied by respondent No.2, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 1/4th i.e., 5%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.15,500/- x 12 x 11 x 5/100 = Rs.1,02,300/-.
21.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

(SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 1,02,300-00 2.
Pain and
Sufferings 20,000-00 3. Attendant charges, extra 20,000-00
nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4.

Medical Expenses 53,109-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 20,000-00  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 15,500-00  period Suresh B.L vs Ravi M.J on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83288824/
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,30,909/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Regarding liability:- Despite service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absence and was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared and filed objections and contested the matter, but not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove its defence.
On the date of accident policy was in force.

Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and (SCCH-3)
15 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.2 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,30,909/- (Rupees Two lakhs thirty thousand nine hundred and nine only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2, shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in favour of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.4239/2023 petitioner through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining his bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on system, corrected, initialed and then pronounced by me in open court on 06th day of October, 2025).
(B.S.HONNASWAMY) VII Addl. Judge and ACJM, Bengaluru.
